ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure 14, when a direct current is suddenly passed through the fixed coil, the metal ring at the coil end will be ejected. Now a closed ring is placed at the same position on the left side of the fixed coil. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side is marked “left” and the right side is marked “right”; on the left there is a closed metal ring, and on the right is a fixed coil wound on a smooth insulating rod. Below the fixed coil are connected a power supply and switch S; in the power supply symbol, the long plate on the left is the positive pole. After the switch is closed, conventional current enters the left end of the fixed coil from the positive pole of the power supply through the switch, and then flows along the coil winding toward the right end. Reasoning: According to the winding method of the coil in the figure and the right-hand screw rule, after the current is switched on, the left end of the fixed coil is the N pole. Therefore on the left side of the coil, at the position of the closed ring, the direction of the magnetic field passing through the ring is toward the left; at the instant the switch is closed, the coil current goes from zero to nonzero, and the magnetic flux toward the left increases. By Lenz's law, the induced current in the closed ring must hinder this increase of magnetic flux toward the left, so the magnetic field produced by itself should be toward the right. Use the right-hand rule on the closed ring to judge: viewed from the left side, if the current in the ring is clockwise, the magnetic field produced on the ring axis points to the right. Therefore the direction of the induced current is clockwise.
